entries.status: Inherited research observation or question; read its explicit limits
entries.original_record: 59. **Initiation-critical WTC 7 steel has not been unambiguously authenticated in the reviewed record.** This is an identification and relevance limitation, not a claim that no potentially relevant steel was examined or received. FEMA published a real metallurgical examination of Sample 1 with tentative WTC 7 attribution. The official inventory names four WTC7-labeled components within three numbered items, and the later NIST crosswalk supports receipt of A/W14A and B/W14B as unidentified sections. Their building/member attribution, any link to Sample 1, original location, alteration timing, and structural significance remain unresolved; C12a/b receipt also remains unresolved. These affirmative findings and limits are recorded in the [physical-documentary review](SOURCE-EXCERPTS.md#source-physical). They do not establish a pre-collapse intervention, a complete custody chain, or deception.

entries.title: Does the proposed lower-floor fire sequence reproduce the upper-façade free-fall interval?
entries.status: Inherited research observation or question; read its explicit limits
entries.original_record:
67. **Does the proposed lower-floor fire sequence reproduce the upper-façade free-fall interval?** NIST identifies the sustained uncontrolled fires on Floors 7–9 and 11–13, including Floor 13, while acknowledging approximately 2.25 seconds of essentially free-fall descent of the north face. This spatial separation makes the propagation and loss-of-support sequence a specific quantitative question. It does not establish a contradiction merely because the descending upper structure was above the principal fire floors.

    **The question to preserve:** Does NIST’s specified lower-floor fire damage and ensuing failure sequence actually produce sufficiently extensive loss of support, with the timing and residual forces necessary to reproduce the observed upper-façade acceleration, coherence, and motion? Relevant tests include matched model displacement/acceleration, member-force and contact histories, the failure chronology, and measurement and model uncertainty. This makes explicit the connection implicit in item 9 and historical inventory item 58.

    **NIST’s explanation and the mechanical qualification:** Upper stories need not themselves be heated to descend near gravitational acceleration if their supports fail below them. NIST attributes the interval to negligible support after lower exterior-column buckling. Compatibility with that explanation in principle does not independently validate its particular historical sequence; describing the process as progressive collapse does not replace the quantitative comparison.

    **Force constraint and observation limit:** For a defined fixed-mass body, sustained center-of-mass acceleration near gravitational acceleration requires a correspondingly small net non-gravitational vertical force. Substantial upward resistance cannot coexist with that motion unless physically justified downward forces offset it. A tracked roof point is not automatically that body’s center of mass. The body, interval, relative motion, projection, and uncertainty must be established or bounded. This limitation must be tested, not used to invent unlimited hidden motion or unexplained cancelling forces. The linked project force calculations are conditional analyses of separately identified published motion data, not an independent reproduction of NIST’s exact 2.25-second measurement or a measured historical force history. Neither the spatial separation nor free fall alone establishes simultaneous failure of every column, deliberate intervention, or a conspiracy.

    Sources: [NIST FAQ, questions 8–9 and 32](https://www.nist.gov/world-trade-center-investigation/study-faqs/wtc-7-investigation); [finite-interval force analysis](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/finite-interval-force/report.md); [roof-point and center-of-mass identifiability analysis](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/body-com-identifiability/report.md).

entries.title: Screenwall and west-penthouse ordering differs in the published comparison
entries.status: Inherited research observation or question; read its explicit limits
entries.original_record: 68. **Screenwall and west-penthouse ordering differs in the published comparison.** **AUDIT; matched-event verification remains.** The observation column places the east end of the screenwall below the roofline at 8.5 seconds and the west penthouse at 9.3 seconds; the debris-damage model lists 7.3/7.7 and 6.9/7.3 respectively, reversing their order in the paired views. A uniform clock shift cannot repair a reversal. The paired values represent viewpoints, not uncertainty intervals; feature definitions, sightlines, and occlusion must be matched before a stronger physical conclusion. # UAF G3005 section verification and implications

October 21, 2026. **The available checked files do not establish whether UAF actually modeled G3005 as W21x44 or W24x55 in Figure 3.14.** The W21 caption and rendered annotation, the underlying W24 raster label, and NIST's separate W24 figure labels remain preserved. No native section was inferred from an annotation and no collapse model was run.

G3005 is a **floor beam**, not the Column 79 girder A2001. NIST's Figure 8-22 separately labels that girder W33x130. This distinction matters: uncertainty about one adjoining beam does not, by itself, establish the girder's section or invalidate every Column 79 result.

## Available file checks

The Intel operational-store identity passed. The public Git tree at `a1979eb700276e13e46e67cceff6a0954a55a649` contains 62,740 tracked paths and no candidate ending in the declared ABAQUS/SAP/native suffixes. The expanded, ignore-inclusive physical inventories also found no such standalone candidate:

| Physical research scope | File paths enumerated |
| --- | ---: |
| Active public checkout research directory | 45 |
| Active public checkout investigation directory | 281 |
| Intel operational public research tree | 39,037 |
| Current local Sherlock research tree | 4,364 |
| Retained Sherlock preservation tree | 10,034 |
| Intel operational Sherlock research tree | 9,046 |

These are overlapping storage snapshots, not counts of independent evidence. All six completed without enumeration errors. Exact roots, sorted path-list hashes and suffixes are recorded in [sources.json](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/uaf-g3005-native-section-2026-10-21/sources.json) and [observations.json](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/uaf-g3005-native-section-2026-10-21/observations.json). Symlink destinations and Git internals were not traversed. A small-plaintext native-keyword scan of the active public research/investigation checkout found no candidate. It did not search every historical Git blob, every possible extension, other disks, or proprietary embedded formats.

Five ZIP directories were inspected: the current and retained UAF wrappers, two Motion Lab archive copies and the compartment-data archive. None lists a member with a declared native suffix or a nested archive. The UAF copies are the same 834-byte, one-README wrapper, not the advertised model dataset. The other archives' directory checks do not authenticate their complete payloads; full-file SHA-256 was deliberately omitted for the two 172,774,879-byte copies. The named motion-score GZIP files were not decompressed. See [archive-directory-checks.json](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/uaf-g3005-native-section-2026-10-21/archive-directory-checks.json).

Neither UAF final PDF has an attached embedded file in its PDF embedded-file directory. Thus no hidden INP/CAE/ODB attachment was recovered from the reports. This does not exclude model information in another unexamined representation.

UAF's [official project page](https://ine.uaf.edu/wtc7) still advertises a 256 GB open-data download. That public-release claim and the checked local wrapper are different records. The wrapper refers to a repaired dataset corresponding to the September 2019 draft; the final-report case mapping remains unverified. This followup did not acquire the aggregate dataset or retry an inaccessible archive through another tool. Missing local inputs are not evidence that UAF never released models or that either party concealed them.

## Conflicting representations and case locators

Both preserved final PDFs retain the previously documented Figure 3.14 [PDF-layer discrepancy](https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/b016bd3bf61bc664eb8b69d3e4b1828646c91fcc/investigation/wtc7/c79-and-timing-crosschecks-2026-10-21/README.md):

| Source and location | Directly observed representation | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UAF printed p. 86, physical p. 99, Figure 3.14 caption | W21x44 G3005 | Native geometry or assigned section |
| Same figure, visible vector annotation | `W21x44;  G3005 w/o bracing` | Native geometry or assigned section |
| Same figure, underlying embedded raster viewed separately in the preceding audit | `W24x55; G3005 w/o bracing` | Whether that label is stale or the actual input |
| NIST printed pp. 350 and 354, physical pp. 394 and 398, Figures 8-22 and 8-27 | Floor beams labeled W24x55 | The exact native assignment for the member called G3005, or assignments in later NIST models |

The whole rendered UAF page agrees with its caption; this is **not a visible caption-versus-plot-label disagreement**. Both versions have the same Figure 3.14 raster hash. This followup rechecked those hashes and the W21 text without altering either PDF. The preceding layer audit remains the source for the separate-raster manual transcription and covering vector rectangle.

Complete-page visual inspection identifies the braced Figure 3.11 on UAF printed p. 84 / physical p. 97 as `Model-9_Nonlinear_10s.odb`. Figure 3.14 names `Model-10_Nonlinear_10s_No_Support.odb`. The former locator had already appeared in the Figure 3.4 audit; this followup links it to the braced comparison as well. These are figure locators, not recovered files or proof that only bracing changed between the jobs. Both cases' section definitions are needed.

UAF printed p. 84 attributes W21x44 G3005 and four adjoining W24x55 beams to erection drawing E12/13. NIST's preliminary figures visibly group the floor beams under W24x55 labels. Consequently the UAF section criticism has a **publication-level basis**, independently of UAF's own Figure 3.14. Establishing an actual NIST modeling error still needs the member-specific native definition and applicable drawing/revision chain. The complete E12/13 original was not newly acquired or authenticated in this followup. The previously reviewed Column 79 shop details do not substitute for that floor-beam schedule.

## How the actual section could affect UAF criticism

| What native evidence eventually establishes | Consequence for this specific comparison |
| --- | --- |
| G3005 is W21x44 in the matching Figure 3.14 job | The W21 caption would be supported; a stale W24 raster annotation would remain a possible explanation, not an established editing history. The existing label conflict alone would not show a numerical-model defect. |
| G3005 is W24x55 in that job | The figure would not demonstrate the claimed W21x44 case. That would weaken its use as a quantitatively matched counterexample and require a correctly identified W21 comparison. It would not, by itself, refute the independently documented question about NIST's preliminary-model section. |
| The braced and unbraced jobs use different G3005 sections | Their difference could not be attributed solely to bracing. Section and bracing would need matched controls, even if each individual job ran correctly. |
| Native case or assignment remains unidentified | Both the section and its numerical effect remain unresolved; neither side gains a demonstrated physics result from the access gap. |

Changing a section can change axial and bending stiffness, torsional/warping response, local slenderness, thermal force transfer and the buckling sequence. A larger section can increase both restraint-generated force and resistance; the direction and magnitude of the resulting system effect are not determined from the designation alone. For illustration, free uniform thermal expansion is `alpha * deltaT * L`, whereas an ideal fully restrained elastic axial force is `E * A * alpha * deltaT`. These identities are not calculations of this heated composite floor or of lateral-torsional buckling. No numerical sensitivity or change in collapse outcome is claimed here.

## Result

**Downloaded a 40,096,259-byte native-input/diagnostic package for the strong
Figure 4.8 candidate `Floor 3-47(Damaged)_Penthouse45`, case `ACASE2`.**
The public release route and source screenshot provide a substantially better
case identification than filename guessing. Exact original-run/final-report
equivalence, binary/text agreement and executable completeness remain unverified.
This is an acquired native case candidate, not an independently reproduced result.

The prior report-level limitation now has a concrete native-file test target.
In addition, the acquired companion log reports two negative stiffness
eigenvalues and instability/ill-conditioning warnings in its linear-static run.
The warning must be diagnosed; it is not a physical-collapse result.

This acquisition supersedes the earlier scoped statement that no native UAF
candidate was held. It does not retroactively change what earlier checks found,
and does not establish that including P-delta reverses or confirms UAF's result.

## Requested ranking

The current causal comparison remains a **partial ordering, not a strict ranking
and not equal odds**. A newly acquired model file is not a new historical-cause
measurement. The warning is a model-quality concern, not a completed causal test.

| Requested category | Defensible ranking statement |
| --- | --- |
| Fire-driven collapse generally | Not ordered above or below specified deliberate removal by the current independent findings. |
| NIST's particular sequence | Nested within the fire family, not a separate competing cause. Developed and specifically challenged; its complete historical sequence is not established here. |
| Other fire-driven sequences | No specified substitute has earned a preferred position; possibility alone does not repair NIST's sequence. |
| Deliberate support removal | Not ordered above or below the fire family; mechanical compatibility does not establish the historical removal mechanism. |
| Other/mixed mechanisms | Not ranked until sufficiently specified; not automatically last or assigned negligible probability. |

A subjective fire-first ordering could be constructed by adding a prior favoring
accidental failure over intervention; a removal-first ordering could be constructed
by assuming observed support loss is exceptionally unlikely under plausible fire
conditions. This investigation has not calibrated either decisive premise. Neither
is introduced here merely to satisfy a request for an ordinal list. The stronger
claim-level preference remains UAF's qualified criticism of NIST's demonstrated
fidelity over accepting NIST's entire sequence as independently validated, not
UAF's categorical no-fire conclusion over every credible fire pathway.

## Attributable public source and bounded selection

The [institutional project page](https://ine.uaf.edu/wtc7) advertises study data.
The [project release mirror](https://files.wtc7report.org/) directly links the
[Internet Archive item](https://archive.org/details/uaf.wtc.7.files.repaired).
The archive describes September 2019 draft-study data and a repaired original ZIP.
Repair fidelity remains the uploader's assertion; the source is attributable but
not thereby proven identical to every March 2020 final-report input.

The [public listing](https://archive.org/download/uaf.wtc.7.files.repaired)
offers a 238.3G aggregate ZIP. A bounded ordinary HTTPS request to its exposed
member-listing endpoint succeeded after web-tool fetching failed. It acquired
7,179,891 bytes of HTML, with 21,178 file rows parsed by the documented row format.
No aggregate ZIP or torrent was downloaded. Public direct-member GETs then
returned HTTP 200 and the expected selected-file sizes.

Source selections are preserved in [mapping-selection.json](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-a0176bf9d1bd2c30),
[mapping-selection-02.json](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-b8164c45ceee291b) and
[native-selection.json](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-e1d665b8c72f0e74). The latter records why bulky
intermediates, other numbered models, solver installers and duplicate backups
were not selected. CSI's [input/archive documentation](https://web.wiki.csiamerica.com/wiki/spaces/kb/pages/2003860/Archiving%2Banalysis%2Bmodels)
identifies `.sdb` as the main binary input, `.$2k` as its text backup and `.LOG`
as a useful analysis diagnostic. External input dependencies may still exist;
small file size does not prove completeness.

## Figure-to-case identification

The initial small work summary and catalogs did not identify the three-column
case. The 2019 `B.C. of Progressive Collapse Footage in SAP2000.docx` describes
a separate prescribed motion construction; it was not substituted for Figure 4.8.

The decisive lead is `Progressive Collapse Based On NIST Assumtion.pptx` in
`New folder (7)_WTC7 Reports&Files in 2019`. Its title slide describes a static
analysis. Slide 2's original embedded screenshot displays:

- `SAP2000 v21.0.2 Ultimate 64-bit - Floor 3-47(Damaged)_Penthouse45`;
- `Axial Force Diagram (ACASE2)`;
- displayed units `Kip, in, F`.

Root and a separate prior-informed reader visually compared that full screenshot
to the final report's printed p101 / physical p114, Figure 4.8. Its perimeter and
interior layout and numerous readable leading force values match, including
-3529.41, -3499.57, -3070.92, -3975.85, -3837.61, -3451.44, -2524.23, -2505.28,
-1231.67, -1978.2, -3898.65, -3161.24 and -3072.66. The report figure crops the
interface and adds green circles. Neighboring Figure 4.9 has different values
and marked locations. No pixel-registration or complete numerical transcription
was performed; this is strong graphic-content linkage, not binary-file identity.

The target is **bare `Penthouse45`**, not `Penthouse45_Shell`, `Penthouse46`
or `Penthouse49_Shell`. Similar ordinals are not interchangeable case identifiers.

All four members come from the same 2019 archive directory above. Original

## What the original examination establishes

FEMA 403 Appendix C describes two examined members. Its introduction says Sample 1 appeared to originate in WTC 7; the section heading is more categorical. Its original location within the building was unknown. These are two separate attribution levels, and the heading cannot erase the introduction's qualification. The earlier 2001 JOM letter calls the beam WTC 7 material without that introductory qualifier, but likewise lacks an exact-location identification. These are overlapping reports by the same investigators, not independently authenticated recoveries.[1, C-1][2, opening paragraphs]

For Sample 1, the appendix reports near-surface oxidation and sulfidation, a eutectic reaction, grain-boundary penetration and substantial thinning. It identifies optical/scanning-electron metallography and qualitative energy-dispersive X-ray analysis; Figure C-8 ties spectra to selected regions. The authors infer local exposure approaching 1,000 °C from the microstructure and phase behavior. This is a retrospective local temperature inference, not an in-situ temperature record for the building or its load-bearing columns.[1, C-1 to C-5]

The distinction from Sample 2 matters. Sample 2 is associated with a tower, is described as copper-containing high-strength low-alloy steel, and has a different discussion of sulfides and possible melting. Its micrographs and temperature inference must not be relabeled as independent WTC 7 observations. The appendix's final discussion explicitly leaves the sulfur source, rate and pre-/post-collapse timing open.[1, C-5 to C-13]

The laboratory publication supplies positive evidence for the reported local alteration. It does **not** supply, in the inspected pages:

- A dated recovery photograph with an original-site location and uniquely linked member identifier.

The examined records justify specific further inquiries, but do not establish a connection between a deliberate collapse operation and an identifiable person or physical specimen. They also do not justify dismissing the specimen or the handling problems as imaginary. The distinction is between an affirmative, bounded finding and the additional links needed to explain the collapse.

FEMA's published Sample 1 examination is positive evidence of a reported local metallurgical alteration. Its introduction tentatively attributes the member to WTC 7; its exact original location and the timing of the alteration remain unresolved in the examined record. The later abstract favoring post-collapse alteration is not a reproduced historical exposure. A critique's quotation about limited dissolution in a preliminary trial is a lead to original methods, not a substitute for them. See the [sample report](SOURCE-EXCERPTS.md#source-sample) and its [claim/lead ledger](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-2de31151fd026932).[1]

The DOJ OIG report documents souvenir-taking, inconsistent accounts of permission, management problems and a specific unforwarded communication. Those are affirmative handling concerns. The report also describes mixed building debris and expressly cannot establish that the investigated globe originated in WTC 7. Neither sorting in a WTC 7 area nor the existence of misconduct supplies a missing specimen-custody or mechanism-concealment link. See the [handling-records source audit](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-edc828d1b8f19311).[2]

No new evidence in this pass connects FEMA Sample 1 to the Fresh Kills operation. These are separate lead families until a record actually joins them.

locators.excerpt:
As of October 6, 2026, this research did not locate a publicly accessible final chemical analysis of the samples taken from the Urban Moving Systems van occupied by the five Israeli nationals detained in New Jersey on September 11, 2001. The released scans establish a canine alert, sample collection, and a September 23 report that the final results were pending. Later records establish administrative closure of laboratory leads, but do not identify the chemical finding.

**The supported conclusion is that the result remains unlocated in the public sources examined.** It is not established that the FBI never completed testing, never released a result to any requester, or obtained a positive or negative chemical result.

This investigation concerns the van bearing New Jersey registration JRJ13Y. It does not treat other vans, photography examinations, handwriting examinations, or intelligence trace checks as the same test. It is a research record, separate from the NIST litigation record and current pleading packet. No request, contact, filing, or transmission resulted from this research.

## What the released records establish

| Record | Location | Established fact | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| September 23, 2001 letterhead memorandum | Section 5, PDF pages 43–44; internal page 2 contains the sample paragraph | The van was searched by a trained dog; interior swabs were sent to the FBI laboratory; the memorandum says “Final results are still pending.” | This is a status statement on that date, not the later chemical result. |
| FD-192 evidence inventory | Section 1, PDF page 7; printed July 29, 2003; acquisition date September 12, 2001 | Newark retained fabric, blanket samples, and control swabs associated with JRJ13Y, with identifiable evidence barcodes. | Sample descriptions and barcodes are not laboratory findings. |
| Closing investigative package dated July 10, 2003 | Section 6, PDF pages 38–58; sample account at pages 42–43; administrative instruction at page 53 | The account still describes the dog alert and laboratory submission. Newark was instructed to discontinue outstanding CD-2C and Laboratory Division leads in ACS. | No chemical outcome is stated. The instruction does not distinguish completed examination, cancellation, or administrative closure. |
| Evidence retention memorandum dated April 14, 2004 | Section 6, PDF page 61 | Newark was awaiting a headquarters summary to determine final disposition of retained evidence after closing its inquiry. | This does not identify the disposition or chemical result of these samples. |
| Property memorandum dated February 18, 2005 | Section 6, PDF page 89 | After unanswered property-retrieval notices, the memorandum treats items as abandoned and states that they will be destroyed. | It is not a completed destruction certificate, does not identify the three sample barcodes, and does not establish destruction of a laboratory report. |

The September 23 date is visible on [the original scan of the memorandum](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%205/page/n42/mode/1up); the pending-results sentence is on [the following page](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%205/page/n43/mode/1up). The date and sentence no longer depend solely on the MintPress article’s attribution.

The later administrative instruction appears in [the July 2003 package](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%206/page/n52/mode/1up). Its enclosed narrative [continues the sample-submission account](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%206/page/n42/mode/1up) without stating a chemical result. The removal of the earlier pending-results sentence does not itself establish that testing was completed.

These are scans of apparent FBI records hosted by third parties, not files retrieved directly from an FBI production portal. Their official forms and internal consistency support their use, but the original agency production was not independently certified. Hash checks confirm the downloaded Internet Archive files match that archive’s metadata; they do not authenticate the archive against the FBI’s originals.

## The specific sample identifiers

The [FD-192 inventory](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%201/page/n6/mode/1up) identifies property group **1B4**, the source vehicle **JRJ13Y**, and the owning office **Newark**.

| Item | Sample description | Evidence barcode |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | Fabric submitted as an explosives-residue sample | E01889035 |
| 16 and 17 | Control swabs from an agent’s gloves and bomb suits | E01889036 |
| 34 | Blanket samples collected for explosives-residue examination | E01889037 |

Item 35 is described as vacuuming and grouped with other property under E01889578. The visible inventory does not establish that it was part of the same chemical submission, so it is an additional lead rather than a confirmed laboratory specimen.

The glove and suit samples are explicitly controls. Counting these four item numbers as four confirmed explosives findings is unsupported. The phrase describing a sample’s intended examination also cannot substitute for a test result. The barcode is an evidence identifier; a laboratory accession number linking it to a completed examination remains unlocated.

The cover also routes visual material to an examiner in the Explosives Unit. That routing does not report chemical testing of the swabs. Locations: Section 5, PDF pages 69–71, especially [the specimen list](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%205/page/n68/mode/1up) and [the examination description](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%205/page/n70/mode/1up).

Location: [Section 6, PDF pages 36–37](https://archive.org/details/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%206/page/n35/mode/1up).

The additional 2013 production includes an attached outside narrative mentioning negative explosives tests for a different van incident near Oak Harbor and Whidbey Island, Washington, in May 2002. That passage cannot resolve this New Jersey examination. The attachment’s presence in an FBI file is not agency adoption of its assertions. Conversely, a project-completion or “former client” description by itself does not establish that every separately scoped maintenance duty, punch-list item, warranty obligation, credential, or permission ended. Those are open questions, not evidence that such access continued.

## Source observations, kept separate

1. **1997 issuer filing, accessed through a filing mirror.** Securacom’s September 1997 S-1/A describes an October 1996 $8.3 million contract “as part of” the WTC security upgrade and says several projects, including the WTC project, were expected to be substantially completed in 1997. That is a contemporaneous forecast about a defined project; it is not the contract, a completion certificate, or proof that all security work or access ended in 1997. The copy reviewed is hosted by SEC Info, not the SEC archive. [Securacom S-1/A filing copy](https://www.secinfo.com/dsvRq.834g.htm)

2. **2003 press account of company and filing descriptions.** An archived American Reporter article says Stratesec continued to list New York City’s World Trade Center as a “former client” through April 2001. It also attributes to CEO Barry McDaniel a description of an ongoing “completion contract,” reportedly “not quite completed when the Center went down.” The article does not reproduce the relevant contract, a statement of work, or the underlying filing pages in the copy reviewed. These are two attributed descriptions in one secondary source, not two independent confirmations. [Archived 2003 article](https://www.mail-archive.com/ctrl%40listserv.aol.com/msg102103.html)

3. **2005 retrospective reporting on the 1998 transition.** Margie Burns’s *Washington Spectator* article reports that the company received about $9.2 million from the WTC job from 1996 through 1998; it attributes to former manager Al Weinstein the account that Securacom was “excused from the project” in 1998 because it could not fulfill the work, and says EJ Electric took over the electronic-security work. This is a reporter’s account attributed to a former manager, not a termination notice, final invoice, or transfer/acceptance record. [Article copy](https://informationdissemination.org/archive/pdf/marvin.pdf)

4. **A separate former-employee account in that 2005 article.** The article says Jeff Gallup left Stratesec for Landtek and quotes him describing himself as “intimately involved” with WTC security until September 12, 2001; it reports that the FBI took the WTC visitor database from his office then. This is a claim about an individual’s involvement and the reported location of a database. It does not, by itself, establish that Stratesec still held the contract, that Gallup had WTC 7 access on September 11, or who owned or administered that database at the time.

Prior knowledge of the user's marker and earlier work is disclosed. The source

counterfindings:
**Earlier criticisms that our own investigation narrowed or rejected**

These qualifications belong with the inventory:

- **“NIST denied free fall” is not an accurate description of its final account.** The final treatment recognizes the approximately 2.25-second interval; the remaining question is its mechanical reproduction, preserved in item 67. The draft-to-final history must not be used to erase the final acknowledgment. Source: [NIST FAQ, question 32](https://www.nist.gov/world-trade-center-investigation/study-faqs/wtc-7-investigation).
- **“A36 and A572 were modeled identically” is contradicted for the examined released upper-floor definitions.** The [October 24 material check](SOURCE-EXCERPTS.md#source-grades) compares their complete curves and finds distinct values. The pinned printed-table duplication remains a publication issue, while this result positively supports a publication-error explanation for those definitions. Historical invocation, effective assignments, physical grade validity, and version equivalence are not established; do not retain a claim that these grade-specific definitions are unavailable.
- **“No sensitivity studies existed” is unsupported.** The [structural audit, SC10](SOURCE-LINKS.md#ref-665a18b75415c247) records the 3.5-hour non-collapse control and prescribed-removal cases; the published account also compares debris/no-debris variants. The unresolved issue is adequacy, coverage, and reproducibility, not complete absence.
- **“All temperatures were inflated” is not established.** Repeated coefficients, fire-timing discrepancies, and uncertain inputs do not demonstrate a uniformly upward temperature error. Establish effective solver values, their derivation, and consequences before asserting bias. See items 14–19 and 69–71.
- **“No potentially relevant steel was examined or received” would erase affirmative evidence.** The Sample 1 examination, candidate inventory, and NIST receipt findings must remain alongside their unresolved attribution and custody limits; see revised item 59 and the [physical-documentary review](SOURCE-EXCERPTS.md#source-physical).
- **“Every discretionary modeling choice encouraged collapse” is not supported.** Capacity-enhancing assumptions and formulation-dependent fracture effects are contrary evidence; see items 78, 82, and 88. Their existence also does not prove the model historically accurate.
- **“NIST omitted all residual support” is unsupported.** The reviewed models include bearing, contact, discrete resistance, and retained supports.
- **Suspected connection-table ratio errors were not substantiated after allowing for display rounding.**
- **The seat-dimension erratum does not establish that the simulation used the erroneous printed dimension.**
- **Our proposed seamless join between two CBS clips failed.** It cannot support a continuous fire-duration measurement.
- **Our image work has not produced a defensible burning-window percentage or demonstrated temperature inflation.**
- **UAF’s prescribed broad support failures do not identify the historical cause of those failures.**
- **Other fire-driven pathways remain possible.** Weakening NIST’s exact sequence would not eliminate the entire fire-mechanism family.
- **Near-free-fall façade motion does not by itself identify initiation, whole-building force balance, or intent.**
- **No reviewed anomaly establishes an executed conspiracy or deliberate falsification.**

The strongest objection to treating this as a list of demonstrated failures is that **many entries identify what our available record cannot yet resolve**. Missing replication is weaker evidence than a reproduced contradiction. The highest-value next evidence remains the exact executed runs, paired sensitivity cases, processing histories, and independently testable output—not another accumulation of unexplained-looking details.
